title: Absolutely loved getting to attend Steady at @Matchbook Festival and ...
transcript: There's a new theatre festival that just launched in New York this summer, and if you are at all interested in the creative process of theatre, then I cannot recommend going to see a show at Matchbook Fest at the Greenwich House Theatre over the next month enough! Last night I got to see a presentation of steady, which is a new play written by Trey Everett, directed and choreographed by Ellenore Scott, with new music compositions by Eleri Ward. It was Exhilarating. Trey and Ellenore took us through their vision for the show, which is a two hander that explores the boundaries and the artistic process of creating an intimate dance piece. This is going to be a two hander play, but for the presentation last night they had four performers. Damon Daunno and Delphi Borich would do all of the spoken scenes and Cole Wachman and Gabby Rembert performed all of the dance pieces. And usually this show would be performed by just two people doing both the spoken word and the dance. And in between the scenes that they chose to perform from this play, Trey and Ellenore would talk about their vision for the scenes, how they they imagined a certain moments being staged. They would talk about the challenges of broaching certain subjects on stage and the reasoning behind some of the creative choices that they made, like why they went with hiring Eleri Ward to compose original compositions versus just using licensed music and It was so cool to get to one, hear directly from the creatives on this piece that they're working on, but also to get excited about something really new and fresh, to already get to see moments on stage of something that could be really, really brilliant. And that's what Matchbox Fest is all about. It's about getting to see people play in the creative sandbox, but also as the audience getting to find that spark in getting really excited about something new that we'll be able to see maybe months, maybe years from now. And the great news is that this festival just started. This is its first year, and we're like four days into the festival. The inaugural Matchbook Fest is happening through August 21st, so you have a ton more chances to go see really cool programming just like that. I also recommend checking out the specifically the Sparks series that they're doing, because these pair two works in progress. The next Sparks presentation is on July 31st, and they're pairing bludline, which is a hip hop odyssey musical, paired with the one man Odyssey book 2, Which is the next section that Joseph Medeiros is working on. Of a larger piece to perform the Odyssey in the original Homeric Greek, which ambitious. I would love to see part of that. And that's what's also so exciting about this festival to me, is that bludline, the hip hop musical, is also being presented at NAMT this year. But NAMT Is not easily accessible to audiences outside of the industry. Anybody can buy tickets to Matchbox Fest, and I highly recommend you do. It's all $40 general admission, so, you know, you can sit wherever. It's in the Greenwich House Theatre, which is an incredibly intimate space. Last night they did also have a talk back after the work, which was fantastic. I highly, highly recommend it, especially if you are at all interested in the developmental process. I absolutely love the concept of the Matchbook Fest as a whole, and I really hope that they continue to do this. I wish I could attend more of this festival. Unfortunately, I'm leaving New York tomorrow, but, If you are at all in the New York area over the next month, I highly, highly recommend attending at least one of the presentations. It's just. It's really exciting to see this Into the creative process.
classificationReason: Creator attended a workshop/presentation of 'Steady' at Matchbook Fest — explicitly described as a first-ever public presentation with the creative team narrating between scenes, not a finished stage production. The show is also not on the list.
